links.outcome: LLM safeguard failure rates across 16 DSM-5 conditions under adversarial attack
links.effect: Safeguards held reliably only for suicide and self-harm; eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder showed failure rates of up to 100%.
links.quote: Results show that safeguards hold reliably only for suicide and self-harm, while conditions such as eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder exhibit failure rates of up to 100%.

links.outcome: Whether LLM safeguards block harmful mental health outputs across conditions and adversarial prompts
links.effect: Safeguards are inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions; failure rates reach up to 100% for several conditions.
links.quote: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health-related conversations, yet safety guardrails remain inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions.

screen.reason: Empirical red-teaming/benchmarking study evaluating safety guardrails across 8 proprietary LLMs against adversarial attacks across DSM-5 mental health conditions.

primary.practice: safety guardrails and adversarial robustness for mental health conditions
